# Phase 25.1: Close gap: v1.3 memory runtime and feedback wiring - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-07-02
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Mode:** Auto-generated from v1.3 audit gaps (workflow.skip_discuss=true)

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

This closure phase resolves the critical v1.3 audit gaps before milestone completion. It must wire memory recall into ordinary InkStatute WeCom/runtime submission paths, connect feedback callbacks to safe memory correction/candidate workflows, harden `MemoryUse` evidence behavior, and produce the missing validation/verification artifacts for phases 20-25.

The phase must not rebuild Hermes core, move channel ownership back into Hermes, store raw legal/customer text in memory records, or make any external memory provider a live legal-data dependency.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Runtime Memory Wiring
- Ordinary WeCom continue/start flows must be able to invoke platform memory recall before backend submission.
- The integration must preserve interrupt resume and active-task fast-path behavior from the existing WeCom session runtime.
- Context passed to backend submission must remain bounded and reference-first: memory refs, rolling summary refs, feedback correction refs, artifact refs, and output-policy refs only.
- Backend gateway/meta/session commands must not leak to ordinary lawyer users.

### Feedback-to-Memory Wiring
- Feedback callbacks may create same-session correction refs and pending memory candidates only through privacy-safe, reference-first metadata.
- High-risk legal conclusions, route mismatch, skill candidates, and skill changes must remain human-reviewed and `no_auto_modify`.
- Approved candidates may enter durable recall only through explicit review actions; rejected or deferred candidates must not enter recall.
- Service-level feedback wiring must stay backend-neutral and InkStatute-owned.

### Evidence and Failure Behavior
- `MemoryUse` evidence failure must not be silently ignored in legal production mode.
- The caller must receive fail-closed behavior or explicit degraded status metadata when evidence cannot be recorded.
- Contract logs and memory evidence must avoid raw callback bodies, legal/customer full text, document text, and secrets.
- Evaluation and fixture evidence must remain synthetic or sanitized.

### Verification Closure
- Produce or normalize validation artifacts for phases 22, 23, 24, and 25.
- Produce `VERIFICATION.md` for phases 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25 after closure work is in place.
- Update requirement traceability only when verification evidence exists.
- The v1.3 milestone audit must be rerunnable and no longer report critical runtime/feedback wiring gaps.

### the agent's Discretion
Implementation details are at the agent's discretion when they preserve the V2 platform contract, InkStatute-owned WeCom boundary, privacy rules, and existing codebase patterns.

</decisions>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### Reusable Assets
- `packages/platform-runtime/src/platform_runtime/memory_orchestrator.py` contains `MemoryOrchestrator`, `MemoryOrchestratorPolicy`, and `OrchestratorIsolationError`.
- `packages/platform-runtime/src/platform_runtime/rolling_summary.py` contains the rolling summary producer and trigger policy.
- `packages/platform-runtime/src/platform_runtime/memory_review.py` contains review actions, review store, and `MemoryCandidateReviewDecider`.
- `services/wecom-service/src/wecom_service/session_runtime.py` owns ordinary WeCom session runtime turn handling.
- `services/wecom-service/src/wecom_service/ingress_runtime.py` owns sanitized callback-to-runtime ingress.
- `services/feedback-service/src/feedback_service/` owns feedback normalization, classification, and pending queues.

### Established Patterns
- Platform runtime packages are dependency-light Python library surfaces.
- WeCom service owns user-facing ingress/egress and must filter backend/system notices.
- Runtime evidence should use refs, hashes, lengths, IDs, timestamps, and sanitized metadata instead of raw payloads.
- Existing tests use stdlib `unittest` in platform packages and `pytest` in service packages.

### Integration Points
- Add memory recall before `runtime.create_run` in ordinary WeCom continue/start flows.
- Attach returned context metadata to the existing backend submission path without changing Hermes core.
- Connect feedback classification results to safe correction refs and candidate queues.
- Add tests around session runtime, ingress runtime, memory orchestration, feedback learning, evidence behavior, evaluation, and contract fixtures.

</code_context>

<specifics>
## Specific Ideas

- Use `.planning/v1.3-MILESTONE-AUDIT.md` as the closure source of truth.
- Preserve platform-native memory as the default; external adapters remain sanitized spikes only.
- Prefer optional host injection points over global services or new runtime daemons.
- Keep legal-specific data in `industry_context` or safe metadata, not platform top-level fields.

</specifics>

<deferred>
## Deferred Ideas

- Live production use of hosted external memory services with real legal/customer payloads remains out of scope.
- User-facing memory management UI remains out of scope.
- Automatic legal skill synthesis or legal conclusion modification remains out of scope.
- Live WeCom UAT and the five-workday lawyer trial remain carried human gates.
